For tied embeddings E, adding z_t=h_t+g·LayerNorm(p_t) changes candidate scores to h_t·E_i+g·LayerNorm(p_t)·E_i: an explicit recent-history similarity component. Architectural inference from [SASRec](https://arxiv.org/abs/1808.09781): this bypass can strengthen local preferences, but its benefit requires validation. [LayerNorm](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/2.14/generated/torch.nn.LayerNorm.html) makes pooled-history scale roughly independent of raw embedding magnitude, initially giving norm near √d; it does not normalize candidate embeddings or guarantee matching encoder scale. Log branch norms and score contributions. Specify normalization placement: normalizing the sum changes the encoder path even when g=0.

A sigmoid gate parameter initialized to zero gives g=0.5, not a near-zero contribution. For desired g=ε, initialize its logit to log(ε/(1−ε)); ε=0.01 gives approximately −4.60. Differentiating the [sigmoid](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/2.14/generated/torch.nn.Sigmoid.html), gate gradients contain g(1−g), while branch-parameter gradients scale with g: extreme negative initialization can delay learning. Tied embeddings still receive encoder/output gradients. [ReZero](https://arxiv.org/abs/2003.04887) instead uses a directly learned zero-initialized scalar; initially the scalar can learn while branch-specific gradients vanish. Avoid simultaneously zeroing the scalar and branch output, which can stall both.

Implementation checks: pool only nonpadding positions j≤t within the recent window; never broadcast a whole-sequence pool across training positions. Divide by valid counts, clamp empty denominators, and explicitly zero empty pools after affine LayerNorm. Suggested parity tests: in eval mode, compare training-path candidate logits with predictor scores for identical prefixes; repeat after checkpoint reload through generated predict.py, including all four dataset routes. Check future-token invariance, empty/singleton histories, padding exclusion, finite gradients, gate movement, and candidate-score equality between gathered full-catalog scores and direct scoring.
